newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ committee to reconvene in Kopu case.
newsitem.headline: NZ committee to reconvene in Kopu case.

text.p: Parliament's privileges committee will reconvene next week to hear further submissions as it considers whether former Alliance MP Alalein Kopu can continue to sit in parliament, committee chairman Paul East said on Tuesday.
He told reporters the committee would have to reconvene to finish questioning the Alliance's lawyers.
Counsel for Kopu had also been expected to give evidence but time did not permit this.
"She may now try to fudge and disguise what she has done but the reality is that on three separate occasions she openly and willingly entered into that commitment," NZPA reported.

The Alliance lawyers disputed suggestions by Prime Minister Jim Bolger, who sits on the committee, that Kopu was under duress, having signed the agreement after an eight-hour meeting. Justice Minister Doug Graham, who is also on the committee, questioned how it would be possible to uphold the proportionality of the German-style Mixed Member Proportional system -- also at the centre of the Alliance's case -- for list MPs who had not signed pledges with their parties.
Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters asked whether there were to be two rules for list MPs, depending on whether they had signed pledges or not.
The legal counsel said that that argument did not apply to the Kopu case.
"We're here because of the contract," they said.
The Alliance has alleged that Kopu did not tell the truth in evidence to the committee last week and said it would lodge another complaint with parliament's Speaker.
Kopu stood in the Te Tai Rawhiti electorate in the October 1996 elections but came last in the four-way race, getting just under 6 percent of the vote.
Collins said Kopu was in Parliament "for one and one reason alone and that is because she occupies a place that was reserved, specifically reserved, for those who were on the Alliance list".

"If she was not on that list she could not under any circumstances be in Parliament and her suggestion to you last week that she was considering at the time that she signed the pledges that she would become an ordinary constituent Member of Parliament were nothing less than fanciful and cannot be accepted," Collins told the committee.
